title: Introduction to Google Apps Script
objectives: Explain Apps Script and common Workspace automation uses.
Identify the editor, functions, execution log, and debugging controls.
Create and run a simple logging function in Apps Script.
Explain Google authorization and the CodeLab execution boundary.
introduction: Learn Apps Script editor, JavaScript syntax, bound/standalone projects, functions, authorization, logs/debugging with fictional, student-owned Google Workspace resources.
explanation: Google Apps Script is Google-hosted scripting for Workspace automation using JavaScript. Standalone projects are independent; bound projects belong to a Sheet/Form/Doc and can expose that container context. Create a practice project in the Apps Script editor, select helloCodeLab, and run it there. Logger.log or console.log sends text to the execution log; it does not create a Google Form. Access to Workspace services may require consent; review scopes and use only an account/resources you are authorized to use. CodeLab only stores source and expected results and never grants Google permissions or executes these services.
workspace_setup:
Execution environment: Google Apps Script editor / Google Workspace. CodeLab stores/copies source and never executes privileged Google services.
Create a dedicated practice project using a Google account you are authorized to use; use V8 JavaScript. Keep each lesson in a separate practice project or merge shared helpers deliberately without duplicate declarations.
Required services: Logging only; no Forms/Sheets/Drive/Mail calls.
Review the example, setup, permissions and expected effects before selecting its entry function in Google. For configuration, replace YOUR_FORM_ID/YOUR_SPREADSHEET_ID/YOUR_FOLDER_ID/YOUR_TEMPLATE_DOCUMENT_ID only with your authorized practice resources, usually in Project Settings > Script Properties. No production IDs or passwords belong in submissions.
form_setup: No Google Form is required for this first logging example.
sheet_setup: No Sheet is required. Create a standalone practice script; logs stay in its Executions/editor log.
authorization_note: Execution occurs in your own Google Apps Script account/project. Review requested service scopes and use only resources you are authorized to access. Do not approve unknown scripts, bypass security warnings, or request unnecessary scopes. CodeLab requests no Google OAuth permissions. Installable triggers execute as their creator; additional Forms/Sheets/Drive/Docs/Mail services may require additional consent.
quota_note: Google quotas, email allowances, trigger execution budgets and service limits vary by account and can change. Check current official Apps Script quota documentation and your Executions environment rather than treating lesson numbers as permanent Google limits. Batch calls, guard empty ranges, avoid duplicate triggers/retries, and defer quota failures. Example lock waits and grade thresholds are application choices, not Google quota claims.
